title: Immutable internal LB Terraform orchestrator for VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a Terraform module and deployment orchestration pattern that replaces internal load balancers immutably (create-new-and-swap) to support safe TLS termination, health-driven upgrades, and predictable cutovers for Private (VPC) Redwood deployments. The goal is to avoid in-place LB mutations that cause transient routing or certificate race conditions and to provide a reusable, documented workflow for staging -> canary -> full rollout.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Terraform module allows creation of 'lb stack' with NLB passthrough or ALB TLS termination via inputs. 2) Module emits outputs needed to update internal DNS records and route53 weighted records for gradual cutover. 3) Automated post-deploy health checks (synthetic) validate pod/service readiness and upstream integration before shifting traffic. 4) Rollback path documented and codified as a single script/CI job. 5) Demo completed in staging and verified by SRE and Platform PM.
proposal: Implement an immutable LB pattern: new LB resources (NLB+ALB pair) are provisioned in a new terraform workspace, registered with target groups, and validated before swapping a Route53 weighted record. TLS options: default is ALB-managed TLS (ACM cert attached) with optional NLB TCP passthrough for mTLS or L7 heterogeneous workloads. Key implementation notes: - Use a named prefix (service + build-id) for resource immutability. - Expose inputs: lb_type (alb|nlb), tls_mode (terminate|passthrough), acm_certificate_arn, health_check_path, connection_draining_timeout. - Healthchecks: HTTP /healthz and gRPC probes supported; default interval 10s, timeout 3s, healthy_threshold 3, unhealthy_threshold 2. - Provide outputs: primary_dns_name, route53_weighted_record, target_group_arns, lb_resource_tag. - Maintain an orchestration wrapper (bash + terraform + smoke tests) that can be invoked by CI to perform canary shifts (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
progress_updates: 2026-02-10 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket and initial proposal after workshop with SRE and Platform. Agree to prefer immutable replacements to mitigate certificate swapping races.

2026-02-18 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype module skeleton completed. Verified ALB attach/detach sequence in dev account. Found provider ordering issue when reusing target-group names; switched to unique suffixes per run.

2026-02-22 - Maya Singh (SRE): Ran synthetic health checks against canary deployment. Observed two intermittent 502s during first 5 minutes; root cause traced to target group deregistration delay. Lowered deregistration delay and added connection draining config.

2026-02-26 - Liam O'Connor: Added Route53 weighted record emitter and CI job to automate canary shifts. Implemented smoke test job that verifies /healthz and a representative business endpoint before increasing weight.

2026-03-01 - PM review by Carlos Ramirez: Reviewed rollout docs and accepted approach pending security review for ACM usage across accounts. Marked ready for staged run in staging environment next week.
blockers: Pending cross-account ACM permission for cert import and an open Terraform provider bug that sporadically recreates target groups when tags change (provider issue referenced in PR #621). Need SRE approval for low-level connection draining default (30s -> proposed 60s) and confirmation from Security on KMS key usage for private certs.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy module in staging workspace with lb_type=alb and tls_mode=terminate. 2) Run CI smoke tests (10-minute window). 3) Canary: create weighted route53 record at 10% for 30 minutes with synthetic checks every 15s. 4) If green, increase to 50% for 30 minutes, then 100%. 5) Monitor latency, 5xx ratio, and error budget burn; automated rollback if thresholds breached. 6) After 72h stabilization, decommission old LB resources via same terraform wrapper.
postmortem_and_metrics: Will collect: per-route latency p50/p95, 5xx rate, connection drain tail-latency, and DNS propagation time. If incidents occur, attach postmortem to ticket and create follow-ups for module improvements.
notes: Follow-up tasks: add explicit support for service-mesh sidecar health probes, document required IAM permissions for Route53 and ACM, provide an example KMS-backed cert flow for on-prem customers. Consider adding an option for terraform-managed NLB TLS listener using Network Load Balancer TLS termination when ALB not suitable.
